c.tagline: Where the Hajar Mountains meet the Arabian Sea.

taxi.fareNote: Meters are rarely used; agree the fare with the driver before the ride, or use Careem for a set upfront price.

emergency.note: 9999 is the single nationwide number for police, ambulance and fire in Oman.

hood_landmark.Al Bustan / Bandar Jissah: Al Bustan Palace, a Ritz-Carlton Hotel

avoid.reason: Crime is rare; agree taxi fares in advance and stay out of wadi beds during rain due to flash floods.

hood_desc: Muscat's historic old town: a working port, the atmospheric Mutrah Souq and a curving corniche lined with traditional dhow harbors and the fish market; suits culture-focused travelers and photographers who don't mind being away from the beach.

Muscat's beachfront resort strip lined with 5-star hotels, foreign embassies and upscale seafront dining; ideal for leisure travelers, couples and honeymooners who want sea views and a walkable promenade.
A leafy, expat-heavy commercial hub with Qurum Natural Park, shopping malls and a public beach; a practical, well-connected base for families and mid-range travelers who want amenities close by.

The bustling commercial downtown (CBD) with banks, the Ruwi souq ("Gold Souq") and the largest concentration of budget hotels; suits business travelers and backpackers who prioritize cost and transit links over scenery.

A secluded resort enclave in coves between the Hajar Mountains and the Gulf of Oman, east of the city center; best for luxury travelers and honeymooners seeking seclusion, though a car or taxi is needed for sightseeing.
lodging: Al Bustan Palace, a Ritz-Carlton Hotel

water.note: Desalinated tap water meets international standards, though bottled water is widely preferred for taste.

transit.pay: Fares are paid in cash to the driver in small OMR denominations, or via the Mwasalat mobile app/prepaid card on some routes; exact change is helpful as buses rarely give change for large notes.
transit.hours: Most routes operate roughly 6:00am-10:00pm; there is minimal to no late-night service, so taxis or ride-hailing apps are needed after hours.
transit.note: Coverage and frequency are limited compared to other Gulf capitals; most residents and visitors rely on taxis, ride-hailing (Careem) or rental cars rather than the bus network.

bus: Mwasalat intercity coaches to Salalah, Sohar, Nizwa and Sur
ferry: National Ferries Company routes from Muscat to Khasab (Musandam)

airport.name: Muscat International Airport (MCT)
airport.drive: 30-40 min to Qurum/CBD; 45-60 min to Muttrah or Old Muscat depending on traffic

transit.m: Mwasalat Route 111 Airport Express bus (~45 min)
Official airport taxi counter (fixed pre-paid fare)

tip.r: Not deeply rooted in local custom; rounding up taxi fares and 5-10% at tourist-oriented restaurants is appreciated but never demanded.
